newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Moslem nations to discuss cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Moslem nations to discuss cooperation.

text.p: A Turkish minister on Thursday said presidents of eight mainly Moslem countries will gather in Ankara later this month to discuss economic cooperation.

"The presidents of eight Moslem developing countries will come together to discuss the subject (of cooperation)...on November 27 and decide on an agenda," Environment Minister Ziyattin Tokar told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
A Foreign Ministry official said the meeting would bring together representatives from Turkey, Iran, Pakistan, Egypt, Malaysia, Indonesia, Nigeria and Bangladesh.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has visited all these countries apart from Bangladesh. The Foreign Ministry official told Reuters that plans for the meeting were established during Erbakan's visits.
The official said the planned cooperation among the eight countries would focus on strengthening economic relations.
Erbakan has set out to strengthen secular Turkey's ties with other Moslem countries since coming to power at the end of June.
